judge.review: Independent read-only review, 2026-10-01; did not author these files

rulings:
REJECTED. Exhaustive one-round review against every item of the current judging bar and the vendored spec, published pages, and cached application commits.
O0. Act 0 (frame): the actor table states what each actor holds but omits its grant. Add the organization's full operational grant for the OAT (the scopes of the served operations), Lena's authority over that organization's token and webhook settings, and each buyer's authorization solely over their checkout or customer session. State the environment consistently with the life. Do not give a buyer the organization's token.
O1. Act 1: delete the two authentication refusals. Neither has a cause carried out in the story, and they draw the same authentication cause twice consecutively. Keep the legitimate token issuance and successful biller boot.
O2. Act 2: delete the failed confirmation retry after the successful checkout in the same sitting; the bar explicitly rejects a failing repeat of a request that succeeded earlier in the sitting. Say Ada supplies payment details and starts the trial, without being charged yet (Polar Trials); remove the claim that she pays immediately.
O3. Act 3: establish that Acme first creates its World, then two hours pass before the reported completed world-hours. The current life creates the World at 15:00 but reports hour identifiers for 10:00 and 11:00 on that same day, before the World existed. Retain the successful duplicate-event retry, which does not fail.
O4. Act 4: delete the disconnected Acme Labs duplicate-email refusal. No preceding application action initiates a second organization's customer creation. Keep the Globex missing-session, support intervention and successful retry whose cause is carried out. Correct 'the biller only retries 404' to describe the actual isNotFound check at the cached commit: status 404 OR a message matching not found/404; whether a 422 invokes fallback depends on its actual message.
O5. Act 5: checkout TTL is 24 hours in Polar's published config, read by models/checkout.py get_expires_at, not 1 hour. Make Grace leave the open page for 25 hours before submitting its displayed form; her fresh payment is Wednesday 11 February. Move Heidi to Thursday 12 February, retaining the later 16 April date. Delete the unknown-checkout refusal: the story gives no person or application a cause to manufacture that ID.
O7. Act 7: keep one complete read per resource by the newly rooted World, which does not already hold the organization. Delete the extra customer-email and event-name filtered reads; after complete lists this same actor has no need for them, and they form an option tour rather than refresh work.
All other acts were checked. Sources: docs/contributing/architecture.md What a judge rejects and Writing a life; polar/spec/openapi.json.gz security and Checkout schemas; https://polar.sh/docs/features/subscriptions/trials; https://github.com/polarsource/polar/blob/main/server/polar/config.py CHECKOUT_TTL_SECONDS; https://github.com/polarsource/polar/blob/main/server/polar/models/checkout.py get_expires_at; cached twin-world 96ca4478bb39 apps/billing/src/polar.ts isNotFound/portalFor.
doubts: The customer-life frame calls this a year although it ends in April, and the full life does not show leaving the vendor; this is a scope/wording doubt rather than a ruling under the explicit rejection list.
